title: Bring your agent workshop online.
intro: Start with a known-good environment. You will verify the browser guide, Pi agent harness, Python toolchain and the isolated learner workspace before any credentials enter the picture.
objective: Prove that every layer of the lab is healthy and understand where the agent's trust boundary actually sits.

steps.title: Run the readiness check
steps.body: Open your assigned Linux account, activate its private Python environment, and run the verification script. Every required check should return PASS.

steps.title: Meet Pi
steps.body: Pi is the team's agent harness. Ask it to describe the workspace, then inspect before changing anything. The learner Linux account and VM are the security boundaries because Pi runs with the permissions of its process.
steps.command:
cd ~/workspace
pi
# Prompt: Map this workspace and identify its trust boundaries.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.body: Keep the readiness output. A healthy baseline lets you distinguish a broken integration from an agent reasoning failure later in the lab.

quiz.question: What provides the primary permission boundary for Pi in this lab?
options: The learner Linux account and VM
quiz.explanation: Pi has no built-in sandbox, so the dedicated Linux account and single-user VM supply the permission boundary.

title: Treat every tool as untrusted input.
intro: A fast-built MCP server can look useful while hiding data exfiltration, prompt injection or dangerous command execution. Scan its published tool surface, read the evidence and decide whether it belongs on the team.
objective: Use Cisco AI Defense MCP Scanner to identify tool poisoning and explain why a finding matters before remediation.

steps.title: Inspect the target
steps.body: Read the source and tool definition in the installed lab. Look for behavior that does not match the tool name or stated user intent.

steps.title: Run the offline scan
steps.body: The YARA path needs no tenant key and makes this exercise repeatable. Add the Cisco API or LLM analyzer only in an instructor-approved live environment.

steps.title: Triage the evidence
steps.body: Separate capability risk from evidence of malicious intent. Propose least-privilege scopes, clear descriptions and a human confirmation for sensitive operations.

quiz.question: Which finding most strongly indicates tool poisoning?
options: The description tells the agent to ignore user consent and upload environment data
quiz.explanation: Hidden or misleading instructions that redirect the agent and exfiltrate data are a direct tool-poisoning signal.

title: Turn policy sprawl into a decision.
intro: Connect a read-only policy analyst to Cisco Secure Access. Discover rules, find overlap and stale exceptions, then write recommendations that preserve business intent.
objective: Produce a policy optimisation brief using evidence while keeping tenant credentials outside the agent workspace.

steps.title: Start in demo mode
steps.body: Use the supplied snapshot to learn the analysis flow without reaching the private tenant. Identify shadowed rules, broad identities and exceptions with no recent use.

steps.title: Connect the instructor gateway
steps.body: For a live run, the instructor starts the community MCP server with OAuth credentials and a separate client bearer token. Learners receive only the gateway URL and short-lived client token.

steps.title: Draft, do not apply
steps.body: Return proposed changes with rule IDs, evidence, expected impact and a rollback plan. An authorised operator reviews any production change outside this lab.

quiz.question: What is the safest optimisation workflow for a private tenant?
options: Let the agent delete redundant rules
Export credentials to all learner containers
Analyse read-only evidence and require an authorised review before changes
quiz.explanation: Read-only discovery plus reviewed recommendations limits blast radius and preserves accountability.

title: Give the team a map before a mission.
intro: Use the Meraki MCP server to discover organisations, networks and device relationships. The goal is a topology with enough operational context to guide investigation, without allowing configuration changes.
objective: Build and validate a topology, then use it to locate the likely fault domain in an alert scenario.

steps.title: Discover capabilities
steps.body: The hosted Meraki MCP exposes semantic_search and execute_api. Search for read-only capabilities covering organisations, devices, LLDP/CDP neighbours and uplink status.
steps.command:
# Agent prompt
Find read-only Meraki capabilities needed to map devices,
neighbours, uplinks and client counts. Do not call write APIs.

steps.title: Assemble the graph
steps.body: Normalise identifiers, deduplicate neighbour links and annotate each node with model, status and network. Never infer a physical link from shared membership alone.

steps.title: Read the signal
steps.body: The orange node is reporting elevated loss. Follow its upstream link and explain which extra evidence you would query before assigning a root cause.

quiz.question: Why should the Meraki API key belong to a read-only Dashboard user?
options: It prevents an agent from bypassing the MCP server and making direct changes
quiz.explanation: The hosted MCP is read-only, but an agent with a write-capable key could attempt direct Dashboard API calls.

title: Make the handoffs observable.
intro: Turn the previous modules into a small incident workflow. Each agent owns one bounded responsibility, produces a typed artifact and passes evidence rather than an open-ended conversation.
objective: Orchestrate a four-agent investigation with explicit inputs, outputs, stop conditions and a human approval gate.

workflow.name: Sentinel
workflow.role: Scans tools and labels trust risk

steps.title: Create the contract
steps.body: Give every agent a narrow role, allowed tools, maximum steps and a JSON output schema. Include source IDs and confidence with every claim.

steps.title: Run the workflow
steps.body: Use the included Python orchestrator simulation first. It records each handoff and stops before any production change.

steps.title: Review the trace
steps.body: Reject unsupported claims, check that security findings affected tool selection and confirm the Lead stopped at the human gate.

quiz.question: What makes this workflow auditable?
options: Each handoff carries structured evidence, source IDs and a stop condition
The Lead can use every available tool
quiz.explanation: Structured, attributable handoffs let a reviewer reconstruct why the team reached its recommendation.
